exams.syllabus: Trinity Singing syllabus. Lists read from the board's official repertoire pages.
comps: Face-to-face: Initial-G5: 3 songs at 22 each (66; fluency & accuracy 7, technical facility 7, communication & interpretation 8) + technical work 14 + two supporting tests 10 each (any two of sight reading, aural, improvisation, musical knowledge) = 100. G6-8: 4 songs at 17 each (68; 5/5/7) + technical work 12 + sight reading 10 + aural or improvisation 10 = 100. Technical work is one of: vocal exercises, Vaccai exercise(s), unaccompanied folk song. Distinction 87-100, Merit 75-86, Pass 60-74, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44. No need to pass every section. UCAS points G6 8/10/12, G7 12/14/16, G8 18/24/30 (pass/merit/distinction). Digital technical-work pathway: songs (3 x 22 to G5; 4 x 17 G6-8) + technical work (14, or 12 G6-8) + overall performance 20 = 100; no supporting tests. Digital repertoire-only pathway: 4 songs at 25 each to G5, 5 songs at 20 each at G6-8 = 100.

Initial-G5: 3 songs from the grade lists; from G1, no more than two from any one group; may be translated into English at these grades; any voice type, any key (published or transposed). G6-8: 4 songs, max two per group, at least one from group A, original language unless stated, at least two living languages in programme. Own composition may replace one song (0.5-1 min at Initial up to 4-4.5 min at G8; stave notation G6-8; may self-accompany). Songs with published accompaniment must be accompanied as printed; face-to-face accompanist provided by candidate, recorded accompaniment allowed to G3, live from G4; digital allows backing tracks at all grades (no demo tracks with sung vocal line). Memory optional.

Digital exams are filmed in one continuous take (front view, face, hands and most of body visible) and uploaded. Pathways: technical-work (songs + technical work + overall performance mark, no supporting tests) or repertoire-only (4 songs to G5, 5 songs G6-8). Technical work is performed from memory; accompaniment may be recorded.
sections: Scales & technical work

Choose one option, all from memory: (1) all three Trinity Vocal Exercises (TCL016775): Vocal exercises Sailing (pitch & tone), Beat the Drum (rhythm), Springtime (diction), piano accompanied; (2) Vaccai (Metodo Pratico), in Italian, accompanied: Vaccai Lektion I (The Scale only: Manca sollecita); (3) unaccompanied folk song (Language of Folk 1): Three Jolly Fishermen or Chiall mo làmh a lùths. Any key, transposed consistently.
Sight-reading

Sight singing (three parts: sing interval, clap rhythm, sing melody with examiner's piano; 30 s prep, tonic chord and start note given). Interval test: sing major 2nd from examiner's lower note; clap rhythm; sung 4-bar melody in C major, 2/4, range of a 3rd, crotchets, mf, q=72, scale patterns/repeated notes, 2-part accompaniment.
Aural & other tests

Choose two of: sight reading, aural, improvisation, musical knowledge. Aural (4-bar major melody): clap pulse on 3rd playing; forte/piano; legato/staccato; highest or lowest of first 3 notes. Improv (stylistic/motivic/harmonic): 4 bars, C major, chords I, V. Musical knowledge (questions on own songs, vocal line only): note names, durations, clefs, signatures, basic terms.

comps: Face-to-face: Initial-G5: 3 songs at 22 each (66; fluency & accuracy 7, technical facility 7, communication & interpretation 8) + technical work 14 + two supporting tests 10 each (any two of sight reading, aural, improvisation, musical knowledge) = 100. G6-8: 4 songs at 17 each (68; 5/5/7) + technical work 12 + sight reading 10 + aural or improvisation 10 = 100. Technical work is one of: vocal exercises, Vaccai exercise(s), unaccompanied folk song. Distinction 87-100, Merit 75-86, Pass 60-74, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44. No need to pass every section. UCAS points G6 8/10/12, G7 12/14/16, G8 18/24/30 (pass/merit/distinction). Digital technical-work pathway: songs (3 x 22 to G5; 4 x 17 G6-8) + technical work (14, or 12 G6-8) + overall performance 20 = 100; no supporting tests. Digital repertoire-only pathway: 4 songs at 25 each to G5, 5 songs at 20 each at G6-8 = 100.

Initial-G5: 3 songs from the grade lists; from G1, no more than two from any one group; may be translated into English at these grades; any voice type, any key (published or transposed). G6-8: 4 songs, max two per group, at least one from group A, original language unless stated, at least two living languages in programme. Own composition may replace one song (0.5-1 min at Initial up to 4-4.5 min at G8; stave notation G6-8; may self-accompany). Songs with published accompaniment must be accompanied as printed; face-to-face accompanist provided by candidate, recorded accompaniment allowed to G3, live from G4; digital allows backing tracks at all grades (no demo tracks with sung vocal line). Memory optional.

Digital exams are filmed in one continuous take (front view, face, hands and most of body visible) and uploaded. Pathways: technical-work (songs + technical work + overall performance mark, no supporting tests) or repertoire-only (4 songs to G5, 5 songs G6-8). Technical work is performed from memory; accompaniment may be recorded.
sections: Scales & technical work

Choose one option, all from memory: (1) all three Trinity Vocal Exercises (TCL016775): All in the Dreamtime, Voyage of Columbus, To the Moon, piano accompanied; (2) Vaccai (Metodo Pratico), in Italian, accompanied: Vaccai Lektion III (skips of sixths: Bella prova e d'alma forte); (3) unaccompanied folk song (Language of Folk 1): The Great Silkie or The Four Loom Weaver. Any key, transposed consistently.
Sight-reading

Sight singing (three parts: sing interval, clap rhythm, sing melody with examiner's piano; 30 s prep, tonic chord and start note given). Interval: perfect 4th. 4 bars, D, A, E minor, range 6th, dotted crotchet/quaver, hairpins, breath marks, slurs, sharpened 7ths, q=82, occasional unsupported material.
Aural & other tests

Choose two of: sight reading, aural, improvisation, musical knowledge. Aural (harmonised 4 bars): pulse; major/minor; perfect/imperfect cadence; interval of first two notes (to 6th); bars of rhythm change and pitch change. Improv: 12 bars, G/B minor. Musical knowledge (questions on own songs, vocal line only): modulation to related keys, tonic/dominant triads, full interval names.

exams.syllabus: Trinity Singing syllabus. Lists read from the board's official repertoire pages.
comps: Face-to-face: Initial-G5: 3 songs at 22 each (66; fluency & accuracy 7, technical facility 7, communication & interpretation 8) + technical work 14 + two supporting tests 10 each (any two of sight reading, aural, improvisation, musical knowledge) = 100. G6-8: 4 songs at 17 each (68; 5/5/7) + technical work 12 + sight reading 10 + aural or improvisation 10 = 100. Technical work is one of: vocal exercises, Vaccai exercise(s), unaccompanied folk song. Distinction 87-100, Merit 75-86, Pass 60-74, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44. No need to pass every section. UCAS points G6 8/10/12, G7 12/14/16, G8 18/24/30 (pass/merit/distinction). Digital technical-work pathway: songs (3 x 22 to G5; 4 x 17 G6-8) + technical work (14, or 12 G6-8) + overall performance 20 = 100; no supporting tests. Digital repertoire-only pathway: 4 songs at 25 each to G5, 5 songs at 20 each at G6-8 = 100.

Initial-G5: 3 songs from the grade lists; from G1, no more than two from any one group; may be translated into English at these grades; any voice type, any key (published or transposed). G6-8: 4 songs, max two per group, at least one from group A, original language unless stated, at least two living languages in programme. Own composition may replace one song (0.5-1 min at Initial up to 4-4.5 min at G8; stave notation G6-8; may self-accompany). Songs with published accompaniment must be accompanied as printed; face-to-face accompanist provided by candidate, recorded accompaniment allowed to G3, live from G4; digital allows backing tracks at all grades (no demo tracks with sung vocal line). Memory optional.
None. No theory or lower-grade prerequisite; grades assume confidence in earlier requirements.

Digital exams are filmed in one continuous take (front view, face, hands and most of body visible) and uploaded. Pathways: technical-work (songs + technical work + overall performance mark, no supporting tests) or repertoire-only (4 songs to G5, 5 songs G6-8). Technical work is performed from memory; accompaniment may be recorded.
sections: Scales & technical work

Choose one option, all from memory: (1) all three Trinity Vocal Exercises (TCL016775): The Sleeping Giant, America, A Mango Mystery, piano accompanied; (2) Vaccai (Metodo Pratico), in Italian, accompanied: Vaccai Lektion V (semitones: Delira dubbiosa); (3) unaccompanied folk song (Language of Folk 2): The Wee Weaver or Maid on the Shore. Any key, transposed consistently.
Sight-reading

Sight singing (three parts: sing interval, clap rhythm, sing melody with examiner's piano; 30 s prep, tonic chord and start note given). Interval: major or minor 6th. 8 bars, Bb and D major, G and B minor, range 9th, 3/4, 4/4, 6/8, cresc/dim, modulation to dominant, accidentals, unsupported material; treble or bass clef.
Aural & other tests

Sight reading plus aural or improvisation. Aural (8 bars): time signature, dynamics, articulation, two other characteristics; modulation (subdominant/dominant/relative minor); locate two melody changes. Alternative: improvisation. Improv: 16 bars, F#/C minor, 7ths.

exams.syllabus: Trinity Singing syllabus. Lists read from the board's official repertoire pages.
comps: Face-to-face: Initial-G5: 3 songs at 22 each (66; fluency & accuracy 7, technical facility 7, communication & interpretation 8) + technical work 14 + two supporting tests 10 each (any two of sight reading, aural, improvisation, musical knowledge) = 100. G6-8: 4 songs at 17 each (68; 5/5/7) + technical work 12 + sight reading 10 + aural or improvisation 10 = 100. Technical work is one of: vocal exercises, Vaccai exercise(s), unaccompanied folk song. Distinction 87-100, Merit 75-86, Pass 60-74, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44. No need to pass every section. UCAS points G6 8/10/12, G7 12/14/16, G8 18/24/30 (pass/merit/distinction). Digital technical-work pathway: songs (3 x 22 to G5; 4 x 17 G6-8) + technical work (14, or 12 G6-8) + overall performance 20 = 100; no supporting tests. Digital repertoire-only pathway: 4 songs at 25 each to G5, 5 songs at 20 each at G6-8 = 100.

Initial-G5: 3 songs from the grade lists; from G1, no more than two from any one group; may be translated into English at these grades; any voice type, any key (published or transposed). G6-8: 4 songs, max two per group, at least one from group A, original language unless stated, at least two living languages in programme. Own composition may replace one song (0.5-1 min at Initial up to 4-4.5 min at G8; stave notation G6-8; may self-accompany). Songs with published accompaniment must be accompanied as printed; face-to-face accompanist provided by candidate, recorded accompaniment allowed to G3, live from G4; digital allows backing tracks at all grades (no demo tracks with sung vocal line). Memory optional.
None. No theory or lower-grade prerequisite; grades assume confidence in earlier requirements.

Digital exams are filmed in one continuous take (front view, face, hands and most of body visible) and uploaded. Pathways: technical-work (songs + technical work + overall performance mark, no supporting tests) or repertoire-only (4 songs to G5, 5 songs G6-8). Technical work is performed from memory; accompaniment may be recorded.
sections: Scales & technical work

Choose one option, all from memory: (1) all three Trinity Vocal Exercises (TCL016775): Song of the Sea, Indigo Shadows, Playground Adventures, piano accompanied; (2) Vaccai (Metodo Pratico), in Italian, accompanied: both Vaccai Lektion IV (skips of sevenths: Fra l'ombre un lampo solo) and Lektion VII (roulades: Come il candore); (3) unaccompanied folk song (Language of Folk 2): Sair Fyel'd Hinny or Ho Ho Bonny Lass. Any key, transposed consistently.
Sight-reading

Sight singing (three parts: sing interval, clap rhythm, sing melody with examiner's piano; 30 s prep, tonic chord and start note given). Interval: any major, minor or perfect interval. 8 bars, A and Eb major, F# and C minor, range 10th, 3/4/6/8/9/8, semiquavers, GP, modulation to relative key.
Aural & other tests

Sight reading plus aural or improvisation. Aural (12-16 bars): time signature, dynamics, articulation, three other characteristics; locate three changes (pitch/rhythm). Alternative: improvisation. Improv: 16 bars, C#/F minor, 7ths, 9ths, suspensions.

exams.syllabus: ABRSM Singing / Singing for Musical Theatre Practical Grades. Lists read from the board's official syllabus PDF.
comps: 150 total: three accompanied songs 30 each (90), unaccompanied traditional song 21, sight-singing 21, aural tests 18. Distinction 130-150, Merit 120-129, Pass 100-119 (a pass in each section is not required).

G1-5: three accompanied songs, one from each of Lists A, B, C (G1-3 total maximum programme time 4/5/6 min). G6-8: three songs from any three of the five Lists A (Early & Sacred), B (Art Songs in French & German), C (Art Songs in English), D (Art Songs in Other Languages), E (Opera, Operetta, Musical Theatre & Popular Song). Plus one unaccompanied traditional (folk) song of own choice. All items from memory (except oratorio/cantata/large sacred works); live piano accompaniment from own accompanist (no self-accompaniment); any voice and key, any language or singing translation; listed arrangements mandatory only where marked 'this version only' or arranger in bold. Some songs carry content-warning flags and a few were removed (list numbers have gaps).

Singing can also be taken as an ABRSM Performance Grade: four songs performed as a recital and assessed from a video, with no sight-singing or aural tests. The Grade 5 Theory (or alternative) prerequisite still applies at Grades 6–8.
sections: Scales & technical work

Unaccompanied traditional (folk) song of own choice, from memory, 1-2 min, different from the accompanied songs; any language, any key (first note/key-chord may be given on piano). No scales or technical work.
Sight-reading

Sight-singing: 4 bars, 4/4; C, G, F major; unseen, no words (any vowel or sol-fa); range about a 6th; stepwise 2nds only, no repeated notes; f/p, hairpins; minims, crotchets, quavers, rests. 30 sec preparation, examiner accompanies (key-chord and start note given).
Aural & other tests

A: clap the pulse of a played piece and say whether 2 or 3 time. B: sing back three 2-bar echoes (major, tonic-mediant). C: identify where a pitch change occurs in a 2-bar phrase (near beginning or end). D: questions on dynamics and articulation.

exams.syllabus: ABRSM Singing / Singing for Musical Theatre Practical Grades. Lists read from the board's official syllabus PDF.
comps: 150 total: three accompanied songs 30 each (90), unaccompanied traditional song 21, sight-singing 21, aural tests 18. Distinction 130-150, Merit 120-129, Pass 100-119 (a pass in each section is not required).

G1-5: three accompanied songs, one from each of Lists A, B, C (G1-3 total maximum programme time 4/5/6 min). G6-8: three songs from any three of the five Lists A (Early & Sacred), B (Art Songs in French & German), C (Art Songs in English), D (Art Songs in Other Languages), E (Opera, Operetta, Musical Theatre & Popular Song). Plus one unaccompanied traditional (folk) song of own choice. All items from memory (except oratorio/cantata/large sacred works); live piano accompaniment from own accompanist (no self-accompaniment); any voice and key, any language or singing translation; listed arrangements mandatory only where marked 'this version only' or arranger in bold. Some songs carry content-warning flags and a few were removed (list numbers have gaps).

Singing can also be taken as an ABRSM Performance Grade: four songs performed as a recital and assessed from a video, with no sight-singing or aural tests. The Grade 5 Theory (or alternative) prerequisite still applies at Grades 6–8.
sections: Scales & technical work

Unaccompanied traditional (folk) song of own choice, from memory, 1-2 min, different from the accompanied songs; any language, any key (first note/key-chord may be given on piano). No scales or technical work.
Sight-reading
Sight-singing: 4 bars; adds D major and 3/4; rising 3rds within the tonic chord; dotted minims/crotchets, mf/mp.
Aural & other tests
A: clap pulse, 2 or 3 time. B: sing three 2-bar echoes (major, tonic-dominant). C: identify a pitch or rhythm change in a 2-bar phrase. D: features - dynamics or articulation, and tempo.

exams.syllabus: ABRSM Singing / Singing for Musical Theatre Practical Grades. Lists read from the board's official syllabus PDF.
comps: 150 total: three accompanied songs 30 each (90), unaccompanied traditional song 21, sight-singing 21, aural tests 18. Distinction 130-150, Merit 120-129, Pass 100-119 (a pass in each section is not required).

G1-5: three accompanied songs, one from each of Lists A, B, C (G1-3 total maximum programme time 4/5/6 min). G6-8: three songs from any three of the five Lists A (Early & Sacred), B (Art Songs in French & German), C (Art Songs in English), D (Art Songs in Other Languages), E (Opera, Operetta, Musical Theatre & Popular Song). Plus one unaccompanied traditional (folk) song of own choice. All items from memory (except oratorio/cantata/large sacred works); live piano accompaniment from own accompanist (no self-accompaniment); any voice and key, any language or singing translation; listed arrangements mandatory only where marked 'this version only' or arranger in bold. Some songs carry content-warning flags and a few were removed (list numbers have gaps).

Singing can also be taken as an ABRSM Performance Grade: four songs performed as a recital and assessed from a video, with no sight-singing or aural tests. The Grade 5 Theory (or alternative) prerequisite still applies at Grades 6–8.
sections: Scales & technical work

Unaccompanied traditional (folk) song of own choice, from memory, 1-2 min, different from the accompanied songs; any language, any key (first note/key-chord may be given on piano). No scales or technical work.
Sight-reading
Sight-singing: 8 bars; adds B-flat major and A minor; range about an octave; rising/falling 3rds, cadential rising perfect 4ths, repeated notes; rests, slowing at end.
Aural & other tests

A: clap pulse, 2, 3 or 4 time. B: sing three 2-bar echoes (major/minor, within an octave). C: identify a pitch or rhythm change in a phrase of up to 4 bars. D: features - dynamics/articulation/tempo, and tonality.

exams.syllabus: ABRSM Singing / Singing for Musical Theatre Practical Grades. Lists read from the board's official syllabus PDF.
comps: 150 total: three accompanied songs 30 each (90), unaccompanied traditional song 21, sight-singing 21, aural tests 18. Distinction 130-150, Merit 120-129, Pass 100-119 (a pass in each section is not required).

G1-5: three accompanied songs, one from each of Lists A, B, C (G1-3 total maximum programme time 4/5/6 min). G6-8: three songs from any three of the five Lists A (Early & Sacred), B (Art Songs in French & German), C (Art Songs in English), D (Art Songs in Other Languages), E (Opera, Operetta, Musical Theatre & Popular Song). Plus one unaccompanied traditional (folk) song of own choice. All items from memory (except oratorio/cantata/large sacred works); live piano accompaniment from own accompanist (no self-accompaniment); any voice and key, any language or singing translation; listed arrangements mandatory only where marked 'this version only' or arranger in bold. Some songs carry content-warning flags and a few were removed (list numbers have gaps).

Singing can also be taken as an ABRSM Performance Grade: four songs performed as a recital and assessed from a video, with no sight-singing or aural tests. The Grade 5 Theory (or alternative) prerequisite still applies at Grades 6–8.
sections: Scales & technical work

Unaccompanied traditional (folk) song of own choice, from memory, 1-2 min, different from the accompanied songs; any language, any key (first note/key-chord may be given on piano). No scales or technical work.
Sight-reading
Sight-singing: 8 bars; adds A and E-flat major, E and D minor, and 6/8; rising perfect 4ths (or falling back), rising/falling octaves; semiquaver patterns, dotted rhythms.
Aural & other tests

A: sing or play back a melody (octave range, up to 3 sharps/flats) heard twice. B: sing five notes from score in free time (C, F or G major, within a 3rd either side of tonic). C: (i) features - one of dynamics/articulation/tempo/tonality, plus character; (ii) clap rhythm of an extract and give 2, 3 or 4 time.

exams.syllabus: ABRSM Singing / Singing for Musical Theatre Practical Grades. Lists read from the board's official syllabus PDF.
comps: 150 total: three accompanied songs 30 each (90), unaccompanied traditional song 21, sight-singing 21, aural tests 18. Distinction 130-150, Merit 120-129, Pass 100-119 (a pass in each section is not required).

G1-5: three accompanied songs, one from each of Lists A, B, C (G1-3 total maximum programme time 4/5/6 min). G6-8: three songs from any three of the five Lists A (Early & Sacred), B (Art Songs in French & German), C (Art Songs in English), D (Art Songs in Other Languages), E (Opera, Operetta, Musical Theatre & Popular Song). Plus one unaccompanied traditional (folk) song of own choice. All items from memory (except oratorio/cantata/large sacred works); live piano accompaniment from own accompanist (no self-accompaniment); any voice and key, any language or singing translation; listed arrangements mandatory only where marked 'this version only' or arranger in bold. Some songs carry content-warning flags and a few were removed (list numbers have gaps).

Singing can also be taken as an ABRSM Performance Grade: four songs performed as a recital and assessed from a video, with no sight-singing or aural tests. The Grade 5 Theory (or alternative) prerequisite still applies at Grades 6–8.
sections: Scales & technical work

Unaccompanied traditional (folk) song of own choice, from memory, 1-3 min, different from the accompanied songs; any language, any key (first note/key-chord may be given on piano). No scales or technical work.
Sight-reading
Sight-singing: 8 bars; adds E major, B and G minor; perfect 5ths, falling perfect 4ths; semibreves, ties, phrase marks.
Aural & other tests

A: sing or play back a melody heard twice (octave range, up to 3 sharps/flats). B: sing six notes from score in free time (major, up to 2 sharps/flats; 5th above to 4th below tonic). C: (i) features - one of dynamics/articulation/tempo/tonality/character, plus style and period; (ii) clap rhythm, 2, 3 or 4 time.

exams.syllabus: ABRSM Singing / Singing for Musical Theatre Practical Grades. Lists read from the board's official syllabus PDF.
comps: 150 total: three accompanied songs 30 each (90), unaccompanied traditional song 21, sight-singing 21, aural tests 18. Distinction 130-150, Merit 120-129, Pass 100-119 (a pass in each section is not required).

G1-5: three accompanied songs, one from each of Lists A, B, C (G1-3 total maximum programme time 4/5/6 min). G6-8: three songs from any three of the five Lists A (Early & Sacred), B (Art Songs in French & German), C (Art Songs in English), D (Art Songs in Other Languages), E (Opera, Operetta, Musical Theatre & Popular Song). Plus one unaccompanied traditional (folk) song of own choice. All items from memory (except oratorio/cantata/large sacred works); live piano accompaniment from own accompanist (no self-accompaniment); any voice and key, any language or singing translation; listed arrangements mandatory only where marked 'this version only' or arranger in bold. Some songs carry content-warning flags and a few were removed (list numbers have gaps).
Grade 5 or above in ABRSM Music Theory, Practical Musicianship or a solo Jazz subject required for Grades 6-8; none for Grades 1-5 and no Initial grade.

Singing can also be taken as an ABRSM Performance Grade: four songs performed as a recital and assessed from a video, with no sight-singing or aural tests. The Grade 5 Theory (or alternative) prerequisite still applies at Grades 6–8.
sections: Scales & technical work

Unaccompanied traditional (folk) song of own choice, from memory, 1-3 min, different from the accompanied songs; any language, any key (first note/key-chord may be given on piano). No scales or technical work.
Sight-reading
Sight-singing: 8-10 bars; adds A-flat major, C minor; printed with simple English words (optional, may use vowel/sol-fa); 6ths, occasional chromatic notes; pp, slurs, accents.
Aural & other tests

A: sing or play back the upper part of a two-part phrase. B: sing a melody from score with examiner's accompaniment (octave range, up to 3 sharps/flats). C: identify cadence as perfect or imperfect. D: (i) features - texture or structure plus one other; (ii) clap rhythm, 2, 3 or 4 time.

exams.syllabus: ABRSM Singing / Singing for Musical Theatre Practical Grades. Lists read from the board's official syllabus PDF.
comps: 150 total: three accompanied songs 30 each (90), unaccompanied traditional song 21, sight-singing 21, aural tests 18. Distinction 130-150, Merit 120-129, Pass 100-119 (a pass in each section is not required).

G1-5: three accompanied songs, one from each of Lists A, B, C (G1-3 total maximum programme time 4/5/6 min). G6-8: three songs from any three of the five Lists A (Early & Sacred), B (Art Songs in French & German), C (Art Songs in English), D (Art Songs in Other Languages), E (Opera, Operetta, Musical Theatre & Popular Song). Plus one unaccompanied traditional (folk) song of own choice. All items from memory (except oratorio/cantata/large sacred works); live piano accompaniment from own accompanist (no self-accompaniment); any voice and key, any language or singing translation; listed arrangements mandatory only where marked 'this version only' or arranger in bold. Some songs carry content-warning flags and a few were removed (list numbers have gaps).
Grade 5 or above in ABRSM Music Theory, Practical Musicianship or a solo Jazz subject required for Grades 6-8; none for Grades 1-5 and no Initial grade.

Singing can also be taken as an ABRSM Performance Grade: four songs performed as a recital and assessed from a video, with no sight-singing or aural tests. The Grade 5 Theory (or alternative) prerequisite still applies at Grades 6–8.
sections: Scales & technical work

Unaccompanied traditional (folk) song of own choice, from memory, 1-3 min, different from the accompanied songs; any language, any key (first note/key-chord may be given on piano). No scales or technical work.
Sight-reading
Sight-singing: 8-10 bars; adds F-sharp minor; occasional minor 7ths, chromatic semitones; triplets, semiquaver rests, staccato, rit. then a tempo, pause sign.
Aural & other tests

A: sing or play back the lower part of a two-part phrase. B: sing the upper part of a two-part phrase from score (up to 4 sharps/flats). C: (i) cadence perfect/imperfect/interrupted; (ii) name the two cadence chords (I, IV, V, V7, VI); (iii) modulation to dominant/subdominant/relative minor. D: (i) two features; (ii) clap rhythm, 2, 3, 4 or 6/8 time.

exams.syllabus: ABRSM Singing / Singing for Musical Theatre Practical Grades. Lists read from the board's official syllabus PDF.
comps: 150 total: three accompanied songs 30 each (90), unaccompanied traditional song 21, sight-singing 21, aural tests 18. Distinction 130-150, Merit 120-129, Pass 100-119 (a pass in each section is not required).

G1-5: three accompanied songs, one from each of Lists A, B, C (G1-3 total maximum programme time 4/5/6 min). G6-8: three songs from any three of the five Lists A (Early & Sacred), B (Art Songs in French & German), C (Art Songs in English), D (Art Songs in Other Languages), E (Opera, Operetta, Musical Theatre & Popular Song). Plus one unaccompanied traditional (folk) song of own choice. All items from memory (except oratorio/cantata/large sacred works); live piano accompaniment from own accompanist (no self-accompaniment); any voice and key, any language or singing translation; listed arrangements mandatory only where marked 'this version only' or arranger in bold. Some songs carry content-warning flags and a few were removed (list numbers have gaps).
Grade 5 or above in ABRSM Music Theory, Practical Musicianship or a solo Jazz subject required for Grades 6-8; none for Grades 1-5 and no Initial grade.

Singing can also be taken as an ABRSM Performance Grade: four songs performed as a recital and assessed from a video, with no sight-singing or aural tests. The Grade 5 Theory (or alternative) prerequisite still applies at Grades 6–8.
sections: Scales & technical work

Unaccompanied traditional (folk) song of own choice, from memory, 1-3 min, different from the accompanied songs; any language, any key (first note/key-chord may be given on piano). No scales or technical work.
Sight-reading
Sight-singing: 8-12 bars; adds C-sharp and F minor; diminished 7ths; ff.
Aural & other tests

A: (i) sing or play back the lowest part of a three-part phrase; (ii) identify cadence (perfect/imperfect/interrupted/plagal); (iii) identify the three chords incl. positions. B: sing the lower part of a two-part phrase from score (up to 4 sharps/flats). C: identify modulations (dominant, subdominant, relative minor/major) in two passages. D: describe characteristic features of a played piece (texture, structure, character, style and period).

exams.name: ARSM
exams.full: Associate of the Royal Schools of Music — ABRSM Level 4 Diploma in Music Performance
exams.syllabus: RQF Level 4 (EQF 5), about the end of the first year of an undergraduate course; 90 credits, 54 GLH, 900 TQT
comps: A pass at Grade 8 on the same or a closely related instrument: ABRSM Practical or Performance Grade 8, or an accepted equivalent from another board (for example Trinity, LCM, MTB, Guildhall, RIAM, AMEB or UNISA). No theory prerequisite.

Face-to-face (public venue or private visit) OR digital (video recorded at a time and place of the candidate's choice, with no fixed sessions; video uploaded at booking or within 28 days). Performance only: 30-minute programme (±2 min), timed from the first note to the last. Marks: pieces 30 (60%) + performance as a whole 20 (40%) = 50. Distinction 45–50, Merit 40–44, Pass 34–39, Below Pass 17–33.

At least 20 minutes from the ARSM repertoire list for the instrument, plus up to 10 minutes of own-choice music at Grade 8 standard or above. No written or spoken elements and no other tests (no viva, no programme notes, no quick study). Candidates submit a programme form, or enter programme details online for digital exams.
sections: About the repertoire list

Official ARSM repertoire list for singing, read from the ABRSM PDF (176 entries in 4 sections). The repertoire lists below are presented according to standard voice categories. As well as choosing items from the list appropriate to their voice, candidates may perform suitable items from the lists for other voice categories. The chosen programme must include a minimum of two different languages. All items may be sung in any key suited to the candidate’s voice, except for items from operas, operettas, oratorios, cantatas and sacred works, which must be sung in the keys in which they were written (although original pitch may be adopted in Baroque pieces, if appropriate). For further details of exam programming requirements, please refer to www.abrsm.org/programme-arsm. Own-choice music is also allowed within the programme rules above. Check the board's current list before entering; lists are updated online.
General notes

Pathway as of Oct 2026: ARSM (L4) → LRSM (L6) → FRSM (L7). DipABRSM is withdrawn (last date 31 Dec 2023). The old-format LRSM closed 30 Apr 2024 and the old FRSM closed 31 Oct 2024. All three current diplomas require only Grade 8 in the instrument (ABRSM or an equivalent board for LRSM/FRSM). No Grade 5 or 6 theory prerequisite is stated for any current performance diploma. Under the old syllabus, Grade 5 theory appeared only as a condition on some substitutions. ARSM has no written element. LRSM/FRSM need a written (2,000 / 3,500 words) or spoken-video (10 / 17 min) supporting-evidence submission. Digital exams have no fixed sessions: book, pay and upload any time; for digital ARSM the video goes in at booking or within 28 days. Specific LRSM/FRSM upload windows weren't stated in the spec, which refers to abrsm.org/how-to-book. ABRSM discontinued printed diploma syllabuses, and lists are updated online, so re-check the abrsm.org pages before entering. abrsm.org HTML pages returned redirect errors to the fetch tool, so some details come from the PDFs and ABRSM's Taiwan mirror.
General rules (all instruments)

Both LRSM and FRSM programmes must be balanced and varied: a variety of moods, keys and tempi and at least two pieces or movements contrasting by period or style. Works and movements must be played complete unless the repertoire list says otherwise, and any list-specific instructions must be followed. Music published with an accompaniment must be performed with one; any suitable instrument may accompany provided the candidate stays the main soloist, candidates arrange their own accompanist, and pre-recorded accompaniments are not allowed unless the composer intended them. Memory is not required (but encouraged if it helps). Any edition matching the list entry may be used and own-choice music must exist as a legible, fully notated score; performing from unauthorised photocopies of copyright editions is not allowed. Own-choice may include the candidate's own composition or arrangement but must still be at or above the required standard, and ABRSM cannot give prior approval of own-choice standard. An audience is encouraged but not required. Infringements (wrong length, too much own choice without approval, wrong movements, edited video) can bring a warning, mark deduction or disqualification. A video can only ever be submitted once, and the same Unit 2 work cannot be reused at a higher level.

exams.name: FRSM
exams.full: Fellowship of the Royal Schools of Music — ABRSM Level 7 Diploma in Music Performance
exams.syllabus: RQF Level 7, about master's/postgraduate level; 134 GLH, 2250 TQT, 225 credits
comps: Same as LRSM: Grade 8 (or equivalent, or approved professional experience) in the instrument presented. LRSM is NOT a formal prerequisite under the new spec.

Digital only. Continuous-take video recital of 55 min ±10%. Woodwind may take one break of up to 5 min. Marks and bands are the same as LRSM: 30/30/15 = 75; Distinction 68–75, Merit 60–67, Pass 50–59.

At least 50% from the FRSM list; own choice up to 50% (about 27 min) at or beyond LRSM standard. Unit 2 supporting evidence (same four options; analysis option covers a 30-min section): 3,500 words ±10% written OR a 17-min ±10% spoken video. No viva voce and no quick study.
sections: About the repertoire list

Official FRSM repertoire list for singing, read from the ABRSM PDF (269 entries in 5 sections). Repertoire may be performed by any voice or gender, and in any appropriate key, except for operas, operetta, oratorios, cantatas and sacred works, which should be sung in the written key (original pitch may be adopted for Baroque pieces). Programmes should include items in at least two different languages. Own-choice music is also allowed within the programme rules above. Check the board's current list before entering; lists are updated online.
General notes

Pathway as of Oct 2026: ARSM (L4) → LRSM (L6) → FRSM (L7). DipABRSM is withdrawn (last date 31 Dec 2023). The old-format LRSM closed 30 Apr 2024 and the old FRSM closed 31 Oct 2024. All three current diplomas require only Grade 8 in the instrument (ABRSM or an equivalent board for LRSM/FRSM). No Grade 5 or 6 theory prerequisite is stated for any current performance diploma. Under the old syllabus, Grade 5 theory appeared only as a condition on some substitutions. ARSM has no written element. LRSM/FRSM need a written (2,000 / 3,500 words) or spoken-video (10 / 17 min) supporting-evidence submission. Digital exams have no fixed sessions: book, pay and upload any time; for digital ARSM the video goes in at booking or within 28 days. Specific LRSM/FRSM upload windows weren't stated in the spec, which refers to abrsm.org/how-to-book. ABRSM discontinued printed diploma syllabuses, and lists are updated online, so re-check the abrsm.org pages before entering. abrsm.org HTML pages returned redirect errors to the fetch tool, so some details come from the PDFs and ABRSM's Taiwan mirror.
General rules (all instruments)

Both LRSM and FRSM programmes must be balanced and varied: a variety of moods, keys and tempi and at least two pieces or movements contrasting by period or style. Works and movements must be played complete unless the repertoire list says otherwise, and any list-specific instructions must be followed. Music published with an accompaniment must be performed with one; any suitable instrument may accompany provided the candidate stays the main soloist, candidates arrange their own accompanist, and pre-recorded accompaniments are not allowed unless the composer intended them. Memory is not required (but encouraged if it helps). Any edition matching the list entry may be used and own-choice music must exist as a legible, fully notated score; performing from unauthorised photocopies of copyright editions is not allowed. Own-choice may include the candidate's own composition or arrangement but must still be at or above the required standard, and ABRSM cannot give prior approval of own-choice standard. An audience is encouraged but not required. Infringements (wrong length, too much own choice without approval, wrong movements, edited video) can bring a warning, mark deduction or disqualification. A video can only ever be submitted once, and the same Unit 2 work cannot be reused at a higher level.
Other components

Unit 2 is a written submission (3500 words, plus or minus 10%, PDF) or a spoken video presentation (17 minutes, plus or minus 10%) on one of four options: Informing your audience, Detailed analysis, Programming your performance, or Preparation for performance, based on substantial personal research and reflection. Same format, translation/subtitle and declaration rules as LRSM. First page of each own-choice piece is uploaded as PDF.

N. Boulanger: Legendary teacher of composers such as Copland and Glass; also a composer, conductor and organist.
A. Gibbs: English composer and teacher best known for his songs, notably settings of Walter de la Mare.
Barab: American composer of chamber operas and cellist.
Meyer, Leslie & Goetz: George W. Meyer, Edgar Leslie & E. Ray Goetz
Songwriters of the 1917 hit 'For Me and My Gal'.
Leveridge: English bass singer and composer of theatre songs.
Price: First African-American woman to have a symphony performed by a major US orchestra.
M. R. Lang: American composer of songs and choral music, one of the first women to be performed widely in the US.
P. Cornelius: German composer and poet, known for songs and the comic opera The Barber of Baghdad.
arr. G. Williams: Welsh composer, wrote orchestral, choral and vocal works.
Trad., arr. Cuney Hare: American musician and writer who collected African-American folk songs.
Webern: Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School, known for concise, spare music.
de Castillon: French composer, pupil of Franck, died young.
Falla: Foremost Spanish composer of his era, blending Andalusian folk music with modern French influences.
Lalo: French composer best known for the Symphonie espagnole and his cello concerto.
Marcello: Venetian nobleman, lawyer and Baroque composer of sonatas and psalms.
Richard & Robert Sherman: The Sherman Brothers, songwriters for Disney films like Mary Poppins.
Puccini: Italian opera composer of La Boheme, Tosca and Madama Butterfly.
Trad. Brazilian: Traditional Brazilian folk melody of anonymous origin, here in a modern educational arrangement.
Wolf: Late Romantic composer celebrated for his art songs.
Finzi: English composer of lyrical, pastoral music, especially songs and works for strings.
C. Floyd: American opera composer, known for Susannah.
Mancini & Mercer: Composer and lyricist of the Oscar-winning song Moon River.
Daniel: American songwriter and Disney composer; wrote Lavender Blue.
Cesti: Italian Baroque opera and cantata composer.
Tchaikovsky: Russian Romantic composer of ballets, symphonies and concertos full of memorable melody.
Bennett: Versatile English composer of concert music, film scores and jazz, equally at home in modernist and popular styles.
Moeran: English composer influenced by folk song and the landscapes of Norfolk and Ireland.
Unaeb: Composer of the African song listed; little detail known.
Chausson: French Romantic composer, best known for his Poème for violin.
arr. A. Hopkins: English composer who arranged folk songs for voice and piano.
Gasparini: Italian Baroque composer and teacher of opera and chamber cantatas.
Trad., arr. Althouse: American folk song arranged by Althouse.
Heneker: English composer of Half a Sixpence.
Andersson, Ulvaeus & Rice: Benny Andersson, Björn Ulvaeus and Tim Rice
Swedish ABBA songwriters and lyricist Tim Rice, creators of the musical Chess.
Weill & Anderson: German-American composer and playwright of Lost in the Stars.
Weill & I. Gershwin: Composer and lyricist partnership behind the Broadway musical Lady in the Dark.
Rothschild: German banking-family member and amateur composer of Lieder.
Trad., arr. Kennedy-Fraser: Scottish singer who collected and arranged Hebridean songs.
Lindley: Songwriter or composer of children's and school songs; little biographical detail available.
Arens: Composer of educational string pieces published by Trinity and self-published; details not confirmed.
Hatton: English composer and singer of songs.
Yates: Contemporary composer or arranger of graded teaching music for wind instruments.
attrib. Stradella: Italian Baroque composer of cantatas, oratorios and arias.
Kitt & Miranda: American composers who co-wrote the music of Bring It On: The Musical.
Anon., attrib. Rosa: Italian painter, poet and musician; songs attributed to him are often of uncertain authorship.
Trad., arr. Vaughan Williams: Traditional, arranged by Ralph Vaughan Williams
English composer who collected and arranged English folk songs.
Carter: Composer of percussion solos including Saëta for timpani.
T. A. Arne: English composer of theatre music, songs and 'Rule, Britannia!'.
Kent & Burton: Songwriters of 'The White Cliffs of Dover' (1941).
Nelson: British string teacher and author of many popular method books for young violinists, violists, cellists and bassists.
C. W. Orr: English composer of art songs, many on Housman.
Previn: German-born American conductor, pianist and composer.
di Chiara: Italian composer of Neapolitan-style popular songs.
Libby Larsen: American composer of accessible, rhythmic and lyrical music.
Cilea: Italian opera composer, best known for Adriana Lecouvreur and L'Arlesiana.
Lilburn: Leading New Zealand composer of symphonies and songs.
Stanford: Irish-born composer and teacher in Britain.
Glanville-Hicks: Australian composer who lived in Europe and the USA.
Trad., arr. Stanford: Traditional, arranged by Charles Villiers Stanford
Irish composer and teacher who arranged Irish folk songs.
Sondheim: American composer and lyricist of Sweeney Todd and A Little Night Music.
Anon. ( attrib. Henry VIII): Court music attributed to the Tudor king, a composer and patron of music.
L. Bernstein & Stephen Sondheim: Composer-lyricist team of West Side Story.
Ballard & Stewart: Songwriters behind the 2011 musical Ghost, music by Dave Stewart and Glen Ballard.
Patricia Williams: Contemporary British composer of art songs and vocal music.
Duparc: French composer who left a small but treasured body of mélodies.
Trad., arr. Appleby & Fowler: Traditional tune or folk song, arranged for school and exam use.
Kern & Hammerstein: Composer and lyricist of Show Boat (1927), a landmark of the American musical theatre.
Thorne: Contemporary composer or arranger of graded teaching music for wind instruments.
Harrison: Contemporary composer or arranger of graded teaching music for wind instruments.
Newly & Bricusse: Songwriting team behind Stop the World, I Want to Get Off and Gonna Build a Mountain.
R. Schumann: German Romantic composer of poetic piano cycles, songs and symphonies.
Granados: Spanish pianist and composer, famous for his Spanish Dances and Goyescas.
Stravinsky: Hugely influential composer of The Rite of Spring and later neoclassical works.
R R Bennett: English composer of concert works, film scores and jazz-influenced pieces.
Dray: Composer of a sacred cradle hymn.
Pauline Viardot: Celebrated mezzo-soprano, composer and teacher at the centre of 19th-century European musical life.
Menotti: Italian-American opera composer,  Amahl and the Night Visitors.
Schönberg: French composer of musicals Les Misérables and Miss Saigon.
Kaldalóns: Icelandic composer and physician, famed for lyrical songs.
M. Williamson: Australian composer, Master of the Queen's Music, wrote operas and songs.
Einarsson: Icelandic composer and conductor who wrote many Romantic songs.
Menken: American composer of Disney film musicals including The Little Mermaid, Aladdin and Pocahontas.
Massenet: French opera composer, known for Manon and Thaïs.
de Falla: Foremost Spanish composer of his era, blending Andalusian folk music with modern French influences.
Frank Wildhorn & Leslie Bricusse: Wildhorn composed the musical Jekyll & Hyde; Bricusse wrote its lyrics.
Churchill: American composer for Disney, wrote songs for Snow White, Bambi and Dumbo.
Bonds: African American composer and pianist who set Langston Hughes poems.
Margoshes: American composer of Fame the Musical.
Bononcini: Italian Baroque composer and cellist, who worked in Rome, Vienna and London.
Vinci: Italian Baroque composer of Neapolitan opera.
Burtch: Welsh composer of choral and vocal works, much loved by young singers.
Harline & Washington: American film songwriters who wrote When You Wish Upon a Star and I've Got No Strings for Pinocchio.
Trad., arr. Quilter: Traditional song arranged by Roger Quilter.
Schütz: Leading German early-baroque composer of sacred vocal music.
Roussel: French composer, ex-naval officer, with a vigorous, colourful neoclassical style.
Roe: Composer and teacher known for songs, choral works and educational pieces.
Fain: American composer of Disney songs from Alice in Wonderland and Peter Pan, and many Broadway shows.
Dell’Acqua: Belgian composer, known for her coloratura song Villanelle.
Dunhill: English composer and teacher, writer of chamber and light orchestral works.
Rachmaninov: Russian pianist-composer famed for lush late-Romantic melody.
Wildhorn: American composer of Jekyll & Hyde and The Scarlet Pimpernel.
Stephen Flaherty & Lynn Ahrens: Broadway team of Ragtime and Seussical.
Trad., arr. Harty: Irish conductor and composer who arranged Irish folk songs.
Thiman: English organist and composer of choral and church music.
Schoenberg: Austrian-American composer who developed twelve-tone technique.
W. H. Anderson: Composer and arranger of educational songs.
Trad. South American/Sholom Secunda: Yiddish theatre composer who wrote 'Dona, dona' (1940).
Jonathan Dove: Composer best known for operas such as Flight and choral music.
Vivaldi: Venetian Baroque composer and violinist who wrote hundreds of concertos, including The Four Seasons.
Thorsteinson: Icelandic composer or arranger of a folk-style song.
Trad., arr. Ayres: Traditional tune or folk song, arranged for school and exam use.
Juan del Vado: Spanish Baroque composer of songs and sacred music for the court.
Vine: Australian composer of orchestral, piano and film music.
Somervell: English composer and music educator, known for song cycles such as Maud.
Lloyd Webber: English composer of Cats, Phantom of the Opera and Joseph.
Legrenzi: Italian Baroque composer of operas and sacred works.
arr. Holloway: Arranger of traditional songs for voice and piano.
